title: Semantic Pack L1_079 — travelling
description: A corrected multilingual Progressive Language pack for Travelling.

sourceTopic.title: 079 — Travelling
sentenceGoals: How does the tourist get to the city?
How does the traveler get to Japan?

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: How
Wie
grammarExplanation: German question words often trigger verb-second order.

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: Comment
grammarExplanation: French question words can start a sentence.

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: ¿Cómo
grammarExplanation: Spanish question words carry an accent.

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: 怎麼
grammarExplanation: Chinese question words stay in the same position as the answer.

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: どうやって
grammarExplanation: Japanese question words take particles like が or を.

en.text: How does the tourist get to the city?

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: How → does → the → tourist → get → to → the → city?
grammarExplanation: English word order: question word + auxiliary + subject + main verb.

de.text: Wie kommt der Tourist in die Stadt?

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: Wie → kommt → der → Tourist → in → die → Stadt?
grammarExplanation: German verb-second order in questions.
Question word + verb + subject + rest.

fr.text: Comment le touriste arrive-t-il à la ville?

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: Comment → le → touriste → arrive-t-il → à → la → ville?
grammarExplanation: French questions: question word + verb + subject + complement.
Inversion may be used in formal French.

es.text: ¿Cómo llega el turista a la ciudad?

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: ¿Cómo → llega → el → turista → a → la → ciudad?
grammarExplanation: Spanish questions: question word + verb + subject.
Question words carry a written accent.

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: 遊客 → 怎麼 → 去 → 城市？
grammarExplanation: Chinese word order stays the same in questions.
Question words replace the information being asked about.

ja.text: 観光客はどうやって街に行きますか？

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: 観光 → 客 → は → どう → や → って → 街 → に → 行きますか？
grammarExplanation: Japanese keeps the verb at the end in questions.
The か particle marks a question.
